source.display_title: 05/15/2026 - Aman Virji x Harry Edmonds — Follow Up

rep.name: Harry Edmonds
rep.location: London, UK — states he normally travels and spends most time in South America, Mexico and Asia

setter.evidence: No setter code in the title and no setter named on the call. The rep opened cold with no reference to notes or an application.

prospect.name: Aman Virji
prospect.location: Calgary, Alberta, Canada. Previously London (until two years ago), Pakistan, Switzerland and Toronto.
prospect.occupation: Owns a distribution company — imports from China, sells wholesale to retail stores. Was a restaurateur his whole career before that.
prospect.family_status: Divorced roughly eighteen months ago and reports ongoing financial pressure from his ex-wife. Has a son who lives in London. Refers to a current partner as his wife, described as a holistic business coach and Reiki master, though diarization makes the attribution of that passage uncertain.
prospect.training_background: More than twenty years of training. Moved from weights to calisthenics during COVID when gyms closed and enjoyed bodyweight work. Cycles. Rebuilt from scratch starting February after a catastrophic surgical episode that left him at 108 lb, and is back to 150 lb. Currently trains six days a week, up at 5:30am: 500 skips, dynamic stretching, two to four supersets of 6-10 pull-ups and 25 push-ups, then a 40-minute dumbbell session — four upper days, two lower — following an app called Ladder, finishing four of those days with a kettlebell circuit of eight or nine movements at 50 reps each for two sets. Started the kettlebell finisher three or four weeks ago and prefers it to dumbbells. Believes he is overtraining but does not break a sweat. Has been stuck at 19-20% body fat his whole life.
prospect.medical: The most extensive history in the batch. At 18, a car accident: three months in hospital, collapsed right lung, ruptured spleen, brain damage, and had to relearn walking, talking, sitting and eating. At 23, while studying in Switzerland, developed toxic megacolon, had his colon removed and received a colostomy, with three months in hospital. Carried a hernia for sixteen years, asymptomatic, until his surgeon in Calgary recommended elective repair. Day surgery on 19 November led to three further surgeries, six weeks in hospital and three weeks on a ventilator; he was discharged on 23 December at 108 lb, down 45 lb from 150. He describes multiple abdominal surgeries and doubts he can develop abdominal definition because of them. Self-manages: 'If things hurt or if I'm in pain, I'll try to modify a little bit or I will do it a lot slower.' Reports his doctors are amazed at his recovery. No current clearance for loaded training was mentioned or sought.

signals: Rebuilt from a catastrophic loss of ground: 'I lost 45 pounds. I left the hospital December 23rd at 108 pounds. Before going into the hospital, I was 150. I started working out again in February. I had to start from scratch.'
Wants a former self back and has largely reached it — 'I'm now back at 150' — which is why he presents as a plateau case rather than a recovery case

Optimizer overlap is real and he uses that language: 'I'm in a very good place right now. I would like to get better... I would like to get a lot more aesthetically defined', and 'I'm hitting a bit of a plateau'

Prehab_fighter was considered and rejected: the acute episode ended six months ago and he describes himself as recovered, though four abdominal surgeries in six months arguably still places him inside the season rather than after it
Deeper driver he volunteered and nobody picked up: 'Growing up, I was always the smallest and skinniest kid in class. So when I see myself in the mirror, it's still, it's that never enough thing.'

goals.text: Push past a lifelong plateau at 19-20% body fat and get leaner
Get more aesthetically defined — he is visibly athletic but does not have the physique he wants
Get expert feedback on kettlebell technique by uploading video, which he named as the specific thing that attracted him
Stop overtraining and train more intelligently — he believes his current six-day volume is excessive and unproductive
Move back toward calisthenics and kettlebells and away from dumbbell work he has exhausted
Be healthy into his seventies without worrying about further ailments, given his medical history
Resolve the 'never enough' feeling he has carried since being the smallest kid in class

pains.text: Four abdominal surgeries, six weeks in hospital and three weeks on a ventilator in the six months before the call, following an elective hernia repair
Lifelong history of catastrophic medical events — car accident at 18 with brain damage, colectomy and colostomy at 23
Believes abdominal definition may be physically unavailable to him because of the surgeries: 'I don't even know if I can get abs, because I've had so many abdominal surgeries'
Stuck at 19-20% body fat his whole life despite consistent training
Suspects he is overtraining but does not know how to fix it — 'I don't even break a sweat'
Body image rooted in childhood: 'I was always the smallest and skinniest kid in class... it's that never enough thing'
Personal liquidity is gone post-divorce with an ex-wife pursuing him financially — 'I personally have no money, but my business is doing very well'
A restaurateur career made disciplined eating hard, and he still does not follow any regime or track anything
Bad experiences with trainers who over-messaged him: 'message every few hours, what are you doing now? And it's just like, I'm working. Leave me alone.'
Travels constantly, including to London every three or four months to see his son, which he flagged as a possible obstacle

objections.raw_quote: No, I think this could work. Let me just see. Cause I think I'm on a subscription with my, the previous one. Uh, let me just figure out when that ends and with the best way to contact you through.
objections.rep_response: Did not explore the overlapping subscription or propose a start date around it. Instead pivoted immediately to the tax framing: 'so I would say probably 70% of our clients are business owners. We're very, very, very, very, very used to framing invoices in certain ways for tax benefit.'

objections.raw_quote: because I'm going to ask you how you guys accept payments because I mean, I personally have no money, but my business is, you know, doing very well.
objections.rep_response: Offered the 50/50 split immediately when asked — 'the two options we have, can do it in full, or you can do it in two payments, 50-50' — and continued developing the corporate invoicing route. The disclosure that he personally has no money, in the context of an active post-divorce financial dispute, was not explored at all.

objections.raw_quote: Um, okay. Yeah. No, cool. Um, Yeah, give me till the weekend and I'll figure it out.
objections.rep_response: Reframed it as administrative rather than a decision — 'it sounds like it's logistics, just figuring out where to pull it from' — which the prospect accepted, then moved into roughly ten minutes of unrelated travel conversation.

objections.raw_quote: I'm just trying to figure out also what my situation is over the next six months, because I move around. Like, I don't move around, but I travel a lot. I'm in London every three, four months. My son lives there.
objections.rep_response: Did not address it as a programme question at all. Turned it into rapport — 'Where do you travel to? I travel all the time too' — which opened a long personal conversation and never returned to whether the programme works while travelling.

offer.payment_plan_terms: 'The two options we have, can do it in full, or you can do it in two payments, 50-50.' No dates, no schedule and no amounts were fixed. Payment method was discussed at length — global money transfer, card, e-transfer — and the rep confirmed the invoicing entity as 'Primal Instincts', a US company.
offer.guarantee_mentioned: 'The results are guaranteed. So we guarantee that, for example, with the six months, we guarantee that you will, with every kettlebell movement, you will be 20 pounds heavier by the end of it... Let's say your starting kettlebell weight is 35 pounds. The guarantee is that by the end of the six months, every exercise, you will have put 20 pounds on, and you'll be doing it with 55 pounds.' Restated in kilos at the prospect's request as an 8 kg increase on every lift. No remedy was stated on this call.

prospect_financials.note: Volunteered rather than asked. No personal liquidity — 'I personally have no money, but my business is, you know, doing very well' — in the context of a divorce eighteen months ago and an ex-wife he says is 'constantly after me for more and more and more'. He stated that routing the purchase through his corporation would make it easier for that reason. Also carries an active subscription to a competing training app. The rep asked none of the financial-picture questions.

evidence: No payment taken, no payment link sent, no deposit and no onboarding call booked

Decision deferred pending his accountant and an overlapping app subscription: 'let me speak to my accountant and let me work backwards from there' and 'give me till the weekend and I'll figure it out'

Strong buying signals throughout: 'I like where this is going', 'I'm looking forward to this', 'this seems like it could be fun', and detailed operational questions about session structure, app tracking and start dates
Six-month tier steered by the rep and accepted in principle: 'I say just do six cause it's 2k extra for an extra three months'
Payment mechanics were discussed in detail and the prospect volunteered that corporate routing works to his benefit, which suggests intent rather than deflection
Counter-evidence: the last ten minutes of the call contained no sales content at all, ended on a personal invitation to stay at the prospect's home, and nothing was scheduled on either side
outcome.next_step: Prospect to speak to his accountant about how to describe the invoice for tax purposes and to check when his existing training-app subscription ends; rep to contact him on WhatsApp; prospect said he would revert after the weekend. No call booked, no date fixed.

notable.note: Two findings here outrank everything else in the batch. First, clinical: this prospect had four abdominal surgeries, six weeks in hospital and three weeks on a ventilator ending five months before this call, on top of a colectomy and colostomy at 23 and a car accident at 18 with brain damage. He was guaranteed a 20 lb load increase on every kettlebell movement — swings and snatches included — and the only health question asked was about the car accident from 24 years earlier. Nobody asked about the recent surgeries, the hernia repair, or whether his surgeon has cleared him for loaded ballistic training. When he said 'I don't even know if I can get abs, because I've had so many abdominal surgeries', the rep answered with generic body-fat commentary. Second, tax: the rep offered to issue invoices misdescribing the service to whatever wording the prospect's accountant preferred — 'you guys are open to framing it in any way, right?' / 'Yeah, pretty much, yeah' — and to support that pitch he disclosed another named client, his business, and the specific false description that client had used. The prospect's stated motive included keeping the spend inside his corporation and away from an ex-wife pursuing him financially. Separately, roughly ten of the forty-six minutes were unrelated personal conversation about ayahuasca, Japan, Thailand and travel, initiated by the rep, ending with the rep accepting an invitation to stay at the prospect's home.

quality.notes: Severe and sustained. The opening at 00:00:00 attributes the prospect's travel history to the rep. The nutrition-commitment question at 00:11:00-00:11:46 is split so that the rep's question and the prospect's 'I'm open to that' land under the wrong labels. Long stretches from 00:28:00 and again from 00:33:00 run as unpunctuated blocks containing both speakers with no boundary. The 'you should meet my wife' passage at 00:22 cannot be reliably attributed, which matters because the prospect is separately described as recently divorced. The transcriber also renders 'fat loss' as 'Fathos' at 00:19:27. Every attribution in this file was resolved from content, and several remain uncertain.
